title: Xanthe and the Garden
premise: Xanthe, a nonbinary thief who harvests and sells memories as charms in the walled city of Vell, has spent five years hiding their magic since the kingdom outlawed it. When the border wards collapse on the night the stars go out, Xanthe discovers both catastrophes stem from the same source: a parasitic entity called the Verdant King, which wears the true king's crown and feeds on stolen memories to grow its garden across the land. Hunted by the usurper's inquisitors and haunted by memories of their own that don't belong to them, Xanthe must ally with a disgraced ward-keeper and a rebel archivist to reach the capital and unbind the king before the usurper's armies swallow the free cities. In the end, Xanthe defeats the Verdant King not by destroying it but by giving back every memory it stole—including their own most painful one—freeing the king at the cost of forgetting the person they love, though the final chapter hints that love outlasts memory.
about_author: Marguerite Zhou is the pen name of a former botanical archivist who spent a decade cataloguing heirloom seeds before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about gardens, grief, and the things we trade to survive, and lives with an unreasonable number of ferns.

chapters.title: The Charm Seller's Hours
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. We meet Xanthe selling memory-charms in Vell's night market: a widow's wedding day, a soldier's last sunset. Establishes the price of survival—each sale leaves Xanthe carrying fragments of strangers' lives. Emotional beat: weary tenderness masked by merchant's cynicism.

chapters.title: What the Wards Kept Out
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. A routine theft from a noble's memory goes wrong when Xanthe glimpses something impossible inside it: a green light behind the king's eyes. The city's ward-keepers are questioning thieves. Beat: first cold drop of dread.

chapters.title: Ilsa of the Broken Circle
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Ilsa Vane, disgraced ward-keeper, patrols the failing border wards she once maintained. She finds a hairline crack singing with vegetal magic—and a message carved in old royal cipher. Beat: guilt sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The border wards fall; every star vanishes at once. Panic floods Vell. Xanthe's own stolen memories begin whispering to each other. Beat: awe curdling into terror as the world's rules visibly break.

chapters.title: Refugees and Rumors
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Survivors pour into Vell claiming the countryside is blooming out of season—flowers where villages stood. Xanthe recognizes the description from a stolen memory five years old. Beat: the past arriving like a debt collector.

chapters.title: The Archivist in the Cistern
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Xanthe seeks out Juniper Sable, a rebel archivist hiding banned histories beneath the city. Juniper confirms the pattern: this happened once before, a century ago, and was erased from record. Beat: reluctant alliance formed over forbidden knowledge.

chapters.title: Inquisitor Hale
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. The usurper's chief inquisitor arrives in Vell hunting 'memory-mongers.' Hale is not a fanatic but a true believer in law after chaos—a mirror to Xanthe. Beat: the hunter introduced as sympathetic, making him more dangerous.

chapters.title: A Charm Gone Wrong
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Selling charms to feed refugees, Xanthe accidentally transfers a memory of the Verdant King's garden into a buyer, who begins sleepwalking toward the gates. Xanthe realizes their stolen memories are infected. Beat: horror—their livelihood is a vector.

chapters.title: Juniper's Ledger
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper deciphers the old royal cipher: the Verdant King is a parasite bound to the monarchy itself, fed by a century of quietly harvested memories. The free cities are next. Beat: stakes crystallize from mystery to countdown.

chapters.title: Raid on the Cistern
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Hale's inquisitors raid Juniper's archive. Xanthe escapes with the ledger but watches Juniper captured, buying time with a memory-burst that stuns the squad. Beat: guilt and fury; the cost of survival made flesh.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Bargain
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Ilsa intercepts fleeing Xanthe, intending arrest—but the ledger proves her order knew about the Verdant King and buried it. She offers passage instead of chains. Beat: trust extended across old wounds.

chapters.title: Out Through the Garden Gate
chapters.summary: Xanthe and Isla slip through Vell's sewers as martial law falls. Aboveground, the world is wrong: orchards fruiting in winter, roads swallowed by hedgerows that move. Beat: claustrophobic escape opening onto uncanny wonder.

chapters.title: The Village That Forgot Itself
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. They find a village alive but hollow—people smiling, unable to name their children. Xanthe returns one memory from their stock and watches a woman weep herself whole. Beat: the thesis dramatized—memory is identity, and identity is worth any price.

chapters.title: Hale's Interrogation
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. Hale questions Juniper, who weaponizes truth: showing him records of his own superiors' complicity. Hale's certainty cracks for the first time. Beat: antagonist humanized; doubt planted.

chapters.title: Memories That Aren't Mine
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Around the fire, Xanthe confesses the deeper secret: among their stolen stock are vivid memories of a life they never lived—a lover named Wren, a house by the sea. Either someone planted them, or Xanthe stole their own past. Beat: vulnerability; the mystery turns inward.

chapters.title: The Hedgerow Road
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. The party fights through animated hedge-labyrinth toward the capital. Ilsa reveals she helped build the border wards—and that the plans came from the palace, meaning the fall was sanctioned. Betrayal at the highest level. Beat: righteous anger.

chapters.title: Wren
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. In a waystation they find Wren—alive, older, working for the resistance. Wren claims to know Xanthe intimately; Xanthe remembers nothing. Wren explains: Xanthe sold their own memories to buy Wren's escape from the purge five years ago. Beat: devastating revelation—the price of survival already paid, unknowingly.

chapters.title: What I Bought You With
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Flashback woven through present: reconstructing the sacrifice piece by piece from others' accounts. Xanthe grieves a love they can't feel. Wren refuses to be a stranger again. Beat: heartbreak held at arm's length.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Army
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. Marching with the army, Hale sees the Verdant King's heralds harvesting memories from conquered towns wholesale. His report is confiscated; his aide disappears. Beat: the law he serves revealed as the monster's hand.

chapters.title: Free Cities Council
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The free cities' council debates surrender versus resistance. Xanthe demonstrates the infection via charm, forcing action—but the council demands proof the king still lives beneath the parasite. Someone must go to the palace. Beat: politics as friction; volunteers step forward.

chapters.title: Training the Untrained
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Preparing a small strike team, Ilsa teaches hedge-magic countermeasures while Xanthe trains allies to carry and return memories safely. Found-family warmth before the storm. Beat: brief, earned hope.

chapters.title: Juniper Freed
chapters.summary: Xanthe and Wren's POV. A prison convoy ambush frees Juniper, broken but clutching a stolen page: the unbinding rite requires a memory freely given by someone the king loved. No one knows what the real king loved anymore. Beat: rescue shadowed by an impossible requirement.

chapters.title: The Palace Gardens
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Infiltration through the palace's overgrown grounds, where topiary shapes scream softly. They witness the Verdant King holding court through the monarch's body—beautiful, patient, terrible. Beat: dread at close range.

chapters.title: Audience with the Crown
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Captured and brought before the Verdant King, Xanthe is offered a bargain: all their lost memories returned, Wren's love restored, in exchange for becoming the garden's new keeper. Beat: temptation rendered almost irresistible.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Xanthe refuses—not because they don't want it, but because they've seen what the village-that-forgot paid. Imprisoned in a cell of flowering thorns, they plan escape with Juniper's hidden lockpick charm. Beat: quiet heroism; choosing pain over comfort.

chapters.title: Hale's Choice
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. Ordered to execute prisoners, Hale instead unlocks the cells, citing the law against the crown itself: no lawful king would do this. He joins the fugitives. Beat: antagonist completes arc into ally.

chapters.title: Escape Through Blooming Halls
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. A running battle through the transformed palace. Ilsa holds a corridor alone; Juniper burns the archive-copy of the rite into memory rather than let it burn. Beat: adrenaline, sacrifice, narrow survival.

chapters.title: The King Beneath
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Using their thief's craft, Xanthe slips into the king's buried mind and finds him: an old man dreaming in a garden chair, convinced his captivity is peace. To wake him, someone must give him a memory of being loved. Beat: tenderness inside horror.

chapters.title: The Rite Assembled
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The team gathers components: Ilsa's ward-craft, Hale's legal authority as witness, Juniper's scholarship, Wren's bloodline tie to the old court. But the loving memory remains unfilled. Beat: convergence; the missing piece named aloud.

chapters.title: Wren's Offer
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren possesses the only living memory of loving Xanthe—and realizes the rite could take it. They prepare to give it without telling Xanthe. Beat: dramatic irony breaking the reader's heart.

chapters.title: Counterstroke
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. The Verdant King's armies arrive at the free cities early; the team must act tonight or not at all. Hale buys hours by formally charging the crown with treason before assembled officers, splitting the army's loyalty. Beat: ticking clock; courage in bureaucracy.

chapters.title: Into the Root
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Descent into the garden's root-vault beneath the throne, where a century of harvested memories hangs like lanterns. Xanthe recognizes some as their own. Beat: awe and violation intertwined.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The rite begins. The Verdant King fights back with weaponized nostalgia—showing each ally their dearest memory and offering to make it permanent. Ilsa nearly stays; Hale nearly kneels. Beat: climax's first movement, temptation as combat.

chapters.title: The Memory Given
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren steps into the rite and gives the king their memory of loving Xanthe—the proof that love exists outside the parasite's economy. The old king wakes, weeping, remembering what devotion looks like. Beat: the emotional summit.

chapters.title: What the Garden Took
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The unbinding completes, but the rite's price falls on Xanthe too: returning the king's stolen century means surrendering their own recovered memories, including everything of Wren. The Verdant King, unmade, dissolves into ordinary ivy. Beat: victory inseparable from loss.

chapters.title: Dawn With Stars
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Stars return; wards rekindle under Ilsa's rebuilt design. The freed king abdicates in favor of elected councils in the free cities. Hale begins prosecutions of the complicit. Beat: justice outside the old law, cautiously hopeful.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Door
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Rebuilding in Vell, Xanthe opens a new shop—selling nothing now, just listening. Wren visits daily, a kind stranger who keeps choosing to stay. Xanthe doesn't remember why it matters, only that it does. Beat: bittersweet domesticity.

chapters.title: Seeds
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper catalogs recovered memories for voluntary return, establishing the Archive of Given Things. Some people choose to keep their wounds; the right to forget is honored alongside the right to remember. Beat: thematic resolution—consent as the antidote to theft.

chapters.title: The Garden Tended
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Ilsa walks the former battlefield, now an honest garden, and plants the first ward-tree of the new border—one grown with permission, not plunder. Beat: renewal; the land healed by different hands.

chapters.title: Xanthe and the Garden
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV, closing. Tending a small plot behind the shop, Xanthe finds themselves humming a song they don't know, planting flowers in patterns they don't recognize—Wren's favorites. When Wren takes their hand, something in Xanthe's chest answers before memory can. Love, the book argues, is the one thing that survives being forgotten. Final beat: quiet, earned grace.
